findings.title: Native qbalpe path does not invoke the pressure-overlap balance operator

evidence.observation: qbalpe_stag dispatches to BALCON; BALCON dispatches to leib_sub/qbal_continuity_setup. BALCON imports cloud_bal_wind_modes, not cloud_bal_balance_operator.

The native legacy continuity equation is centered finite differences with one dx(i,j), dy(i,j), and level dp(k), on a global p(nz) grid. It has no pressure-interface overlap segments or pressure_mass_measure.
The separate candidate pipeline calls apply_localized_balance, which uses cloud_bal_balance_operator.

findings.trigger: Run qbalpe_stag on its normal input; the actual BALCON continuity correction follows the legacy staggered leib_sub path, while the candidate pipeline uses the separate A-grid pressure-overlap operator.
findings.equation: Legacy D(u,v,omega) = (u_e-u_w)/dx + (v_n-v_s)/dy + (omega_lower-omega_upper)/dp. Candidate D is assembled from shared pressure-overlap face fluxes, A=M^-1 D S, with M=area*cell_dp/g.
findings.consequence: A closure or manufactured test of cloud_bal_balance_operator does not establish the discrete continuity, adjoint, dry-mass metric, or boundary behavior of the operational/native qbalpe correction. No equivalence result covers varying cell thickness, nonmatching vertical interfaces, or actual native geometry.
findings.next_check: Either route the intended native producer through the pressure-overlap operator with ABI/frame/IO review, or construct an independent native-grid comparison proving legacy-vs-candidate face flux and residual equivalence on actual KLAPS geometry. Then validate the selected path with real native inputs.

findings.title: Wind-mode diagnostics scale the physical increment divergence by influence a second time

evidence.observation: The routine differentiates u1-u0/v1-v0 and then multiplies both divergence and vorticity by influence(i,j,k).
BALCON passes the already-produced candidate wind fields and influence to the diagnostic; the resulting RMS/profile values are printed.
Manufactured mode checks use influence=1 everywhere, so they do not exercise the amplitude bias.

findings.trigger: Use a constant nonzero divergent or rotational increment with influence=0.5 over its diagnostic support. The routine reports half the true discrete mode amplitude; a varying influence also changes the reported spatial mode field without changing u1-u0/v1-v0.
findings.equation: Implemented diagnostic is beta * div(delta u), while mode of the stored increment is div(delta u). If beta is intended as an increment taper, the physical increment itself must be tapered first and then differentiated; otherwise this is an extra factor.
findings.consequence: Printed divergent/rotational RMS and vertical profiles are localization-weighted diagnostics, not the unweighted modes of the accepted output increment. Do not use them as quantitative spatial mass-wind closure evidence. BALCON currently prints them and does not use these values in qbal_candidate_acceptance.
findings.next_check: Clarify metric intent; if it should describe the returned increment, remove the extra weighting and add a beta<1 constant-mode test plus a localized nonuniform-grid fixture.

findings.title: Dry-air divergence remains a diagnostic on the pressure metric, without a dry-mass tendency equation

evidence.observation: state_dry_air_mass_flux_divergence forms dry-air fractions, calls state_continuity_residual with the same pressure volume, and multiplies the result by pressure mass to return D F_d in kg/s.
Interior dry carrier fluxes use pressure-overlap shared faces and interpolate f_d*u or f_d*v; omega vertical flux is multiplied by local dry fraction.
The contract says the routine supplies D F_d only; dot(m_d)+D F_d and native mass-coordinate reconstruction remain open.

findings.trigger: A candidate has nonzero water/hydrometeor loading or differing dry fractions, and a verifier asks whether the wind field conserves dry-air mass. Calling the current routine yields flux divergence, not the complete tendency-plus-flux residual.
findings.equation: The balance metric remains M_p=A*cell_dp/g; the dry-air fraction is f_d=M_d/M_p. The available diagnostic is D F_d. The required closure is dot(M_d)+D F_d=0 with consistent same-carrier native boundaries and tendencies.
findings.consequence: Pressure-mass projection/continuity does not alone certify dry-air mass-wind balance. Boundary dry fraction is also extrapolated from the nearest cell (operator lines 1739-1742), an explicit assumption rather than observed boundary composition.
findings.next_check: Using the same candidate and carrier, reconstruct native dry mass per cell and its physical tendency, replay all shared-face and boundary dry fluxes, and evaluate the complete cell residual on actual native inputs.

no_defect_observed_static: Modern A operator uses paired, oppositely signed shared-face contributions divided by cell pressure mass measure; apply_adjoint_metric matches that operator under its pressure-volume weighted inner product.
Modern solver correction has no top/bottom omega increment faces; the base-state diagnostic includes supplied valid top/bottom omega boundaries and explicit zero-gradient lateral domain fluxes.

Candidate evaluation separately computes geostrophic residual and interior hydrostatic residual. This supports compatibility assessment, but does not establish scientific compatibility on real/native data.
